argument: Through A Happy Death, the unpublished novel Camus wrote just before The Stranger, the episode traces how Camus tested Zagreus's three-part theory of happiness (money, time, solitude), watched monks be happy with almost nothing, and concluded that if happiness is just a matter of will and framing, it can't be the ultimate goal of a serious person. That skepticism reframes Meursault: far from an absurd hero to emulate, he is merely someone in harmony with the particular life he leads, a human embodiment of the absurd whose unrelatability shows that something human is missing, namely revolt. Camus refused to be a philosopher because he saw philosophy's abstractions, fatalism, and realism as the dangerous game that allowed Hitler's rise, and instead made lucidity, not meaning or happiness, the primary focus: continuing to live and care in the absurd tension, without philosophical suicide, is by default an act of revolt.
keyIdeas: Zagreus's theory that happiness lies in money, time, and solitude is not stupid, but Camus's visit to happy monks who had almost nothing revealed that the will toward happiness is the primary factor.

If happiness comes down to how you frame reality, you could be happy while the world burns around you, which made Camus see happiness as a goal only for someone young and avoiding responsibility, a ladder to be kicked away like Wittgenstein's.

The absurd is broader than the desire for meaning: it arises any time something that seems part of our natural constitution, like the desire to know, meets a world that cannot provide it given our limited tools.

Philosophers and religious people, driven to avoid the suffering of living in absurd tension, build systems of abstractions and grand unifying narratives to escape it, a game Camus refuses because he thinks it enabled the rise of Hitler.

Meursault is not an example to emulate but an embodiment of the absurd; what is missing from him, descriptively rather than ethically, is revolt: continuing to live and care while knowing the universe will never provide the meaning you desire.

terms.def: The constant tension created whenever something that seems part of our natural constitution, like the desire for meaning or knowledge, collides with a world that cannot provide it.
Continuing to live authentically and to care within the absurd tension, knowing the universe will never give you the meaning you desire, which is by default what is missing from Meursault.
Escaping the absurd by adopting a grand philosophical justification, religious unity, or narrative rather than affirming reality as it is.
Seeing the world as it is without idealizing, demonizing, or wrapping it in rational abstractions, which Camus makes the primary focus instead of meaning or happiness.
A way of being Camus admired that values joy, the body, and the physical landscape, an embodied immanence in which life itself is enough, symbolized by the sun in his novels.

anchors: someone can have basically NOTHING…and it seems that if their WILL… towards happiness is there…that really DOES seem to be the PRIMARY factor here all things considered.
This STARTS to seem like a goal that someone could ONLY have if they were very YOUNG, AVOIDING responsibility.
and from this new vantage point, that WHOLE conversation you used to be having starts to seem naive…or silly to you.
No to Camus this is JUST someone…who’s achieved a certain kind of HARMONY…with the PARTICULAR life he’s leading.
for Camus the absurd is something we encounter…ANY time, there’s something that SEEMS to be part of our natural constitution as BEINGS, but then we’re met with a world that can’t PROVIDE it for us.

And it’s the avoidance of this personal suffering…this PIECE of what we ARE…well it’s WELL DOCUMENTED that THIS is the origin of the GAME that Camus thinks philosophers and religious people are PLAYING.
He thought the PHILOSOPHERS of his time were lost in abstractions…lost in a type of fatalism and realism that ALLOWED for the rise of Hitler and people LIKE him.
I’m not PLAYING that game. In fact: THAT’S the very kind of GAME…that got us INTO this mess in the FIRST place.

The possibility…of AFFIRMING reality more fully, of affirming the LIFE of this man he’s about to kill…the sun is practically BEGGING him in this moment to engage deeper than his normal level of detachment.
he is not making an ETHICAL claim there…he’s making a DESCRIPTIVE claim.
